method: Compared the lesson with Docker run/none-network docs, Python resource/subprocess docs, gVisor security architecture and Firecracker design. Compiled all three Python fences and ran the extracted L1 demonstration; the local Python 3.14.7 process recovered __import__ through warnings.catch_warnings and only read its PID. On Docker 29.3.1 with the cached python:3.12-alpine image (--pull=never), ran the documented runner/input bind mounts and the read-only/non-root/resource/network probe. The configured none-network run passed five local checks; the default-network comparison exposed a non-loopback default route and failed the read-only/non-root/workspace/host-marker checks as expected. The none-network container also showed extra tunnel device names without non-loopback default routes, so the probe uses route tables rather than interface names. Production build generated 369 pages; Pagefind indexed 369 pages / 15,374 words. Light/dark full-page screenshots were visually reviewed at 1300x11918 with viewport/scrollWidth both 1300, one Mermaid SVG and zero alerts; the initial light load recorded only a favicon.ico 404. The separate repository link checker requested 734 URLs, found no 404/410, and left 19 transient/network-restricted results unverified, including the gVisor docs URL. No provider API calls were made.
limitations: The older L0/L1/L2/L2b timings have no archived per-run logs or complete environment metadata and use different workloads; they remain historical summaries and are not a comparable isolation-overhead benchmark.
The harmless Python object-tree proof demonstrates one blacklist bypass on Python 3.14.7; it is not a claim that all restricted interpreters or versions share the same object graph.

The Docker tests validate one local daemon, one mutable image tag and one configuration. They do not establish production host hardening, multi-tenant escape resistance, image provenance, process-tree cleanup, or deployed egress enforcement.

The L2 subprocess example is a Unix-only local illustration. Python resource limits vary by OS, preexec_fn is unsafe in threaded parents, and the lesson does not validate a production launcher or cgroup policy.
gVisor and Firecracker descriptions were checked against their official architecture documents; neither runtime was installed or benchmarked in this run.
